fields.meta_title: Payroll Change Form With Approvals and Back Pay | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a payroll change form that shows old and new pay side by side, routes raises to the right approver and adds back pay for late changes.
fields.h1: Build a Payroll Change Form With Sign-Off and Effective Dates
fields.hero_description: A payroll change form tells payroll what changes in someone's pay or job, and from which date. Describe who approves what, and Emergent builds the form and its sign-off steps.
fields.features_heading: What Each Change Carries to Payroll
fields.features_subheading: Paper versions record the old pay and the new. Emergent's version also knows who approves each change and when it starts.
fields.feature_1:
Old and new values side by side

Pulls the current rate and title from the employee record, leaving the requester to fill in only what changes. Payroll then reads each old value right beside its replacement.
fields.feature_2:
Effective dates checked against payday

Compares each effective date with your pay calendar. A change dated inside a pay period that has already closed gets marked for back pay and does not drift into a later run.
fields.feature_3:
Approvers picked by the size of a raise

Sends raises under your limit to the manager alone and larger ones to finance too. Each approver gets an email or a Slack message showing the change, with a button to approve it.
fields.feature_4:
A reason code on every request

Asks each requester to pick a reason, such as a merit raise or a promotion. At year end, HR can count how many raises were for merit and how many arrived with a new job title.
fields.feature_5:
Deductions employees start themselves

Lets staff start or stop a voluntary deduction, such as a parking pass, from their phone. Each request carries the employee's signature and a start date before payroll sees it.
fields.feature_6:
The code and the history, yours to keep

Exports the full code to your GitHub repo on paid plans whenever you ask. The change table goes with it, every approval timestamp included, ready for an engineer to extend in-house.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Payroll Changes, Approved and Dated
fields.tab_content_1:
Finance has to sign any raise over 5%

Harbor Point Clinic lets managers approve small raises alone. A manager asks to move a medical assistant to $22.50 an hour from $21.00. The form finds the increase is over 5%, the clinic's limit for manager-only approval. It goes to the finance director, Joan Ellis. Payroll only sees it once she signs.
fields.tab_content_2:
Shipping picks up her labor cost on day one

Copperline Foods runs two warehouse crews, each charged to its own cost center. Rosa Lima, a crew lead, is moving over to Shipping, and both her current and new managers approve the transfer on the form. On the first day of the next pay period, the payroll export charges her hours to cost center 420 instead of 410.
fields.tab_content_3:
A gift to the relief fund, signed from a phone

Westbrook Library offers staff a payroll gift to its employee relief fund. On her phone, Maya Chen picks $10 per paycheck and a start date, then signs. Payroll gets a new deduction line carrying that date, and the form shows her the yearly total: $260 across 26 paychecks.
fields.tab_content_4:
Back pay for 32 hours lands on the next check

Tidewater Kitchens closes each pay run two days before payday. A line cook's raise to $18.25 an hour, up from $17.00, was approved after the run closed, with an effective date already behind it. The form finds 32 hours paid at the old rate and adds $40.00 of back pay to his next check.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Payroll Change Form
fields.howto_description: Payroll needs two facts from every change: the date it takes effect and the name of whoever approved it. Settle how the form gets both before you write the prompt.
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Describe the form in a prompt
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pull last quarter's paper requests and sort them by reason, starting with raises and transfers. The counts show which requests the form should handle on day one and which can wait for a later version.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write down who approves each kind of change. A common split has managers approving raises below a set limit and finance signing anything larger, with HR confirming new titles. State the limit in dollars or percent so the form can apply it.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Give the form your pay calendar with each period's cutoff. A change dated in a period that has closed should show up as back pay. One that arrives after the cutoff should wait for the following run, not slip into the current one.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Tell Emergent which changes the form accepts, who approves each one and where approved changes should go. Emergent sets up the form with approval routing, and every request lands as a row in a database you own.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Connect your payroll provider's API, or export a file in the column order it imports. Approved changes leave with their effective dates attached. Anything still waiting on a signature stays in the table until the last approver signs off.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Decide whether employees get a notice once a change is final. Most teams send a short email naming the new rate and the date it starts. People who see a change in writing before payday come to HR with fewer questions about their check.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Before launch, file one raise under the finance limit and one over it. Then file a change dated in the last pay period. Confirm each one reaches the right approver and that the late one comes back with a back pay line.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is blank paper: a county PDF, two university PDFs, a Scribd amendment sheet, an Office Depot pack of 50 carbon forms, an Etsy salary sheet, a Pinterest board and one Jotform agent template. Every one records an old value, a new value and a signature line, and stops there. None says who approves a raise, what happens when a change lands after the payroll cutoff, or how a transfer moves labor cost. This page shows the form doing that work: a raise over the approval threshold routed to finance, a department transfer that moves the cost center on the effective date, an employee-started deduction change, and a late raise that adds back pay to the next check. The FAQ answers the searcher's questions about corrections, payday and schedule notice, and who owns a payroll error, with federal sources and no advice.

claims_to_source: Federal law (FLSA) lets an employer change work hours without prior notice or consent unless an agreement says otherwise; some state and local scheduling laws add penalties
The FLSA does not set a pay frequency; payday requirements come from state law (DOL state payday table)
An employer remains responsible for federal employment tax deposits even when a payroll service provider handles them
For 2026 the IRS published new withholding methods in Publication 15-T, and for tax years after 2024 and before 2029 P.L. 119-21 allows deductions for qualified tips and overtime
The Social Security wage base changes every year with the national average wage index
